title: Q2 Runway & Pulse: Hosted API + Model Catalog cadence and commitment windows
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable quarterly "Runway & Pulse" cadence for the Hosted API and Model Catalog that (1) aligns cross-functional stakeholders on commitment windows, (2) creates a predictable canary/stabilization schedule for model rotations, and (3) surfaces capacity/hedge requirements and observability milestones.

Why now: Growing model churn and customer demand for predictable SLAs mean we must formalize how we commit model lineups each quarter, surface capacity risk earlier, and measure quality regressions during rollout. This doc defines scope, success metrics, milestones, and handoffs for Q2 planning and first adoption in the April release window.

Deliverables:
- Commitment lanes definition (Canary / Stabilize / Evergreen) and default durations
- Quarter cadence calendar (planning, commit window, canary weeks, final freeze)
- Stakeholder RACI (PM, Eng runtime, SRE, DX, Sales) and meeting cadence
- Canary evaluation checklist & automated dashboards for model health
- Capacity hedge playbook mapping to Dedicated quotas and autoscale rules
- Runbook for rollbacks and emergency fallbacks to compatible variants

Acceptance criteria:
- Cross-functional sign-off from Eng, SRE, DX, and Sales recorded in Confluence
- Canary dashboard (latency/cost/quality) populated for at least two candidate model rotations
- Two-week canary run executed on internal beta cohort with documented metrics
- Capacity hedge triggers wired into alerting and a tested scale-up path

Success metrics (first quarter):
- Mean latency tail reduction during canary < 5% regression from baseline
- No more than 1 customer-facing quality regression per quarter after rollout
- 90% of planned model rotations complete inside the commitment window

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Late infra readiness for quantized model variants. Mitigation: Hard dependency gate with ENG-90321 and earlier integration test run.
- Risk: Canary sample bias. Mitigation: Use stratified traffic split and synthetic prompt sets stored in eval-bench.
- Risk: Capacity oversubscription during peak. Mitigation: Prebook Dedicated burst capacity and implement autoscale guardrails.

Stakeholders and owners:
- PM lead: Maya Chen (assignee)
- Runtime engineering: Jorge Alvarez (primary), eng-owners per model
- SRE/Capacity: Priya Nair
- Observability/DX: Linh Tran
- Sales & CS escalation: Alex Romero

Notes on scope exclusion:
- This ticket does not change pricing or SLA contracts. Those will be coordinated in a separate initiative.
